function: OTFS data detection: an iterative AMP module and GNN recover transmitted QAM symbols in the delay-Doppler domain, with a learned approximation of inter-Doppler interference to cut cost (pp. 1-4).
system: Single-user OTFS, M=64 subcarriers, N=16 slots, 30 kHz spacing, P=4 or 8 paths, QPSK or 16-QAM; antennas and carrier frequency not stated; no RIS (pp. 2, 4).
method: AMP-GNN: AMP module and GNN (MLP messages, GRU updates, T=15 iterations, L=2 rounds) trained with an l2 loss on randomly generated labeled data; supervised, model-driven (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulator: random delay and Doppler indices, Gaussian gains with exponential power profile [14]; training data randomly generated; no standard channel model or measurements (p. 4).
test_conditions: Trained at fixed noise variance per modulation (-15 dB QPSK, -20 dB 16-QAM); tested over SNR, P=4 and 8, QPSK and 16-QAM, perfect and imperfect CSI (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: MP-based [3] and AMP-based [4]. Learned: GNN-based [7] for OTFS. Own variants AMP-GNN-v1 (ignores IDI) and AMP-GNN-v2 (no IDI approximation) as ablations (pp. 4-5).
metrics: BER versus SNR (QPSK and 16-QAM; P=4 and 8; perfect and imperfect CSI); FLOPs (x10^7) and runtime in ms with step decompositions (Table I, pp. 5-8).
complexity: FLOPs and runtime reported: proposed 10.00x10^7 FLOPs, 26.8 ms (P=4) and 14.84x10^7, 28.1 ms (P=8); complexity orders given with FLOP counting in Appendices (pp. 4-8).
openness: none; the only link (p. 5, footnote 2) is the third-party fvcore library used to count FLOPs; no code or data link for the paper itself.
q1_support: p. 4: "A training dataset D is randomly generated" - own simulator with random delay-Doppler indices and Gaussian gains with exponential profile [14]; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 5: "even with imperfect channel state information (CSI)" - tests only sweep SNR, CSI error, number of paths and modulation; the paper never says a trained model is applied to a scenario unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 4: "we simulate three baselines, including the MP-based [3], AMP-based [4], and GNN-based [7] detectors" - MP and AMP are non-learned, GNN-based [7] is the earlier learned OTFS detector; all compared on BER in Fig. 2 (p. 5).
q4_support: p. 5: "Table I compares the complexity of different OTFS detectors in terms of the required number of floating-point operations" - FLOPs and runtime in Table I; complexity orders on p. 4.
q5_support: p. 5: "counted by the fvcore library" - footnote 2 links only a third-party tool for counting FLOPs; the paper releases no code or data of its own and trains on its own randomly generated simulated data.
notes: Read in full from the PDF text (pp. 1-8, including Appendices A to C) and page 5 as an image (Fig. 2, Table I). The PDF is the arXiv:2402.10071v2 preprint 'Approximate Message Passing-Enhanced Graph Neural Network for OTFS Data Detection' (p. 1); it prints no DOI. Area 4: learned detection in the delay-Doppler domain. q3: MP-based and AMP-based are non-learned, GNN-based [7] is the earlier learned detector, compared on BER. q2: the paper trains at one noise variance per modulation and the P=4 and P=8 results are not stated to come from one trained model.
